reading.body:
James Green's 31 AI lobbying filings are concentrated in telecommunications: CTIA, Lumen, Verizon, and AT&T together account for 26 of them.

The client list is the pattern. Wireless carriers and their trade association dominate the record, with IAC and Match Group as the only non-carrier clients named. The bills attached to these filings are almost entirely Senate measures, with three House bills among the twenty entries.

For AI specifically, this matters because telecom carriers are the companies that build and operate the physical network AI depends on. Lobbying on AI by wireless carriers is likely to touch spectrum, data center connectivity, and network infrastructure, though the filings do not say what the lobbying concerned.

The data does not show what was advocated, what the bills would do, or whether any position succeeded. It covers one lobbyist's filings and nothing about the broader lobbying landscape.
